question: A medical student experiences palpitations and visible hand tremor before oral examinations. She has no psychiatric diagnosis. Which pharmacological option is most appropriate PRN for this situational performance anxiety?

answers.text: Propranolol 20 mg oral — blocks peripheral sympathetic manifestations (tremor, palpitations) without sedation or cognitive impairment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Propranolol (non-selective β-blocker) blocks β₁ (cardiac — reduces palpitations, tachycardia) and β₂ (skeletal muscle — reduces tremor) adrenoceptors peripherally. It does not cross the BBB significantly at low doses, so it does not impair cognition or cause sedation — essential for performance situations requiring mental sharpness.

answers.text: Diazepam 5 mg oral — rapid anxiolysis eliminates the physiological arousal causing her symptoms

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Diazepam would reduce anxiety but causes sedation, cognitive impairment, and slowed reaction time — all undesirable during an examination requiring peak mental performance. BZDs are not appropriate for performance situations where cognitive sharpness is needed.

answers.text: Buspirone 10 mg oral — a fast-acting serotonergic anxiolytic ideal for acute situations

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Buspirone has a delayed onset of 2–4 weeks — it is completely ineffective when taken acutely. It is used for chronic GAD maintenance, not for PRN situational anxiety. A single dose before an event provides no benefit.

answers.text: Sertraline 50 mg oral — an SSRI that reduces anticipatory anxiety within hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: SSRIs have a delayed onset of 4–6 weeks for anxiolytic effect. A single dose of sertraline provides no acute anxiety relief. SSRIs are for long-term management of anxiety disorders, not for PRN situational use.

overallFeedback.feedback: For situational performance anxiety: the problem is peripheral sympathetic manifestations (tremor, palpitations) interfering with performance. Propranolol blocks these peripherally without affecting cognition. BZDs cause sedation; buspirone and SSRIs need weeks to work.

Propranolol PRN (20–40 mg, taken 30–60 minutes before) is the pharmacological treatment of choice for performance anxiety because it eliminates visible sympathetic symptoms without cognitive impairment or sedation.
